rules.name: Electives outside of Subplan
rules.desc: Students must complete an additional two courses from any two approved subplan courses other than their own. One course may not count for more than one requirement.

rules.name: Writing in the Major (WIM)
rules.notes: Note: Not all courses are offered yearly.

rules.name: Capstone Experience
rules.desc:
Senior Capstone Project
Students who select to do a senior project for their capstone should enroll in FEMGEN 104X during Spring Quarter of their junior year, followed by FEMGEN 199A in Autumn Quarter of their senior year. Capstone papers must be at least 7,000 words (excluding notes and figures). Creative Capstones may include formats such as short films, podcasts, poetry collections, or performance, and must be paired with a critical written analysis.
All Capstone proposals are reviewed and approved by the FEMGEN 199 instructor(s) and the student’s faculty advisor. Creative projects must meet scholarly standards and clearly articulate their research context, audience, and methodology. Units earned through the FEMGEN 199 series will count toward the major’s unit requirement.
For more information, visit the FGSS website.

children.name: Senior Capstone Project
children.notes: Students must take FEMGEN 104X or an alternative junior year preparation for honors class to allow them to gather data for the thesis over the summer before senior year.

rules.name: Honors Thesis
rules.desc:
Students pursuing honors must complete FEMGEN 199A. In addition, they will complete a minimum of 9 units, including 199A, from the following course list.
Honors Thesis must be a written thesis of at least 15,000 words (excluding notes and figures) that demonstrates original, in-depth research.
Creative Honors Projects are more extensive in scope than a standard senior Capstone project, which may take forms such as a feature-length film, digital media work, or curated exhibition.
All Honors proposals are reviewed and approved by the FEMGEN 199 instructor(s) and the student’s faculty advisor. Creative projects must meet scholarly standards and clearly articulate their research context, audience, and methodology.
Units earned through the FEMGEN 199 series do count toward the major’s unit requirement.

rules.name: Subplan: Humanities and Arts
rules.desc:
The Humanities and Arts subplan centers the arts, history, literature, language, media, and performance in the analysis of how ideas about feminism, gender, and sexuality are developed, produced, and experienced alongside other categories of difference.
Not all courses are offered every year.

rules.name: Subplan: Queer and Transgender Studies
rules.desc:
The Queer and Transgender Studies subplan focuses on the histories, practices, and theories of lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, intersex, and queer identities and communities through multidisciplinary study.
Not all courses are offered every year.

rules.name: Subplan: Technology, Science, and Medicine
rules.desc:
The Technology, Science, and Medicine subplan investigates ethical considerations in how gender, sex, sexuality and other categories of embodied difference shape and are shaped by technology, science, and health and medicine in the application of scientific knowledge.
Not all courses are offered every year.

rules.name: Subplan: Law and Social Sciences
rules.desc:
The Law and Social Sciences subplan investigates how gender, sex, and sexuality and other categories of embodied difference are studied, regulated, and experienced in economics, politics, education, public policy, and the law.
Not all courses are offered every year.

rules.name: Subplan: Individually Designed
rules.desc: Students interested in an individually designed subplan should speak to a prospective advisor from the list of affiliated faculty, and should develop a proposal describing a thematic focus and outlining a course of study. The proposal is then submitted to the Program Office (Bldg. 460, Room 216) for approval by the Director or Associate Director.
